sources.title: Technical accounting training and submission ingestion go-live
Walk with Jackie: what a raise is for

ideas.title: A W-2 is a runway, not a cage
ideas.hook: I enjoy my job. I still want the financial room to say no to an unhealthy work situation.
ideas.hook_alt: Your paycheck can build options. Quitting does not have to be one of them.
ideas.belief_attacked: You have to quit your job to build financial independence
ideas.value_to_listener: Choose how much of a raise can fund greater choice after reserves and debt commitments
ideas.why_it_stops: The first line contradicts what the audience expects from someone selling freedom

outline.beat: The goal is the ability to say no, not a deadline to resign.
Check the surplus after living expenses, debt payments, and reserve needs before assigning a raise.
Compare affordable monthly savings contributions in the calculator. Show the assumptions, not a promised freedom date.
Loop back: the paycheck can build choices, including staying in work you enjoy.

ideas.quote: the new job gives me the morning focus time back, and every extra dollar goes to the machine

ideas.title: Give your raise a job before it disappears
ideas.hook: Got a raise. Where does the first dollar go?
ideas.value_to_listener: Name one priority for affordable surplus before increasing investment commitments
ideas.why_it_stops: A familiar payday decision gives the viewer an immediate action

outline.beat: Slide 1: choose the next priority: reserves, debt, or investment savings.
Slide 2: write the amount left after existing obligations. It does not all have to go into investments.
Slide 3: explore that contribution in /calculator, with a link sticker. Projections depend on assumptions.

ideas.quote: every extra dollar goes to the machine
